segments.intro: Eleven point eight million people live with Parkinson's. Treatment depends on an hour-by-hour paper diary. Most hours stay blank.
segments.hero: Astrolabe reconstructs the missing hours from two wrist sensors.
segments.problem: Even with research staff, just sixty-one point six percent were completed.
segments.reveal: Drag, and the patient's diary appears behind the reconstruction. This participant was held out of training; coverage is measured on held-out people.
segments.refusal: Here is what most demos hide. On this day, the evidence was too weak. So Astrolabe declined all one hundred and fourteen windows.
segments.sensors: Remove one wrist and it does not bluff. It refuses more, holding the same error budget.
segments.voice-before: So tell it what the sensor missed.
segments.voice-after: Transcribed, structured, and confirmed by you. The diary changes. The model's refusal does not.
segments.clinician: It prints for the appointment, and never fills a row it cannot defend.
segments.epidemiology: Parkinson's is the world's fastest-growing neurological condition, and motor fluctuations turn care into a timing problem.
segments.pipeline: Five stages align, extract, model, calibrate, and finally refuse when the evidence is weak.
segments.pick: Choose a participant the model never saw.
segments.posterior: Every hour carries a full probability distribution, not a single confident number.
segments.layers: Turn off inference and see exactly what was observed and reported.
segments.selective: As the detector answers less, accuracy rises from seventy-one point three to eighty-two point five percent.
segments.devices: Only research-grade bilateral wrists expose the raw acceleration this method requires.
segments.report: Every figure in the report regenerates from a named script.
segments.end: Astrolabe. A diary that tells you when it doesn't know.
